title: Blazes ignite at St. Petersburg oil sites as Kyiv launches more than 1,000 drones at Russia
summary: Ukrainian attacks set an oil export terminal ablaze in St. Petersburg on Sunday, as Kyiv launched more than 1,000 drones across Russia in one of its largest ever aerial bombardments.

image.caption: A car burns after a Russian airstrike on a residential neighbourhood in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, on Oct. 17, 2026. (Kateryna Klochko/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Ukrainian attacks set an oil export terminal ablaze in St. Petersburg on Sunday, as Kyiv launched more than 1,000 drones across Russia in one of its largest ever aerial bombardments.
Ukraine targets Russian oil sites, while Russia launches attacks on Zaporizhzhia
The attack comes amid deepening tensions between Ukraine and Washington, with U.S. President Donald Trump criticizing Kyiv for its strikes on Russian oil infrastructure.

One person was killed and five more were wounded in the attack, which sparked fires at both the Petersburg Oil Terminal and the city’s Ruchi oil depot, said local Gov. Alexander Beglov. A logistics centre belonging to Russian retailer Ozon and a data centre for local tech giant VK were also targeted, both companies confirmed.
Russia’s Ministry of Defence said Sunday that its forces had destroyed 1,015 Ukrainian drones over 15 Russian regions, as well as the annexed Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea and the Black Sea.

blocks.text: Meanwhile, a woman died and at least two other people were wounded, including a six-year-old girl, after Russia launched two attacks on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia Saturday, local officials said.
A local man carries carries buckets of broken glass in front a residential building damaged by a Russian airstrike in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, on Oct. 17, 2026. (Kateryna Klochko/The Associated Press)
Two apartment buildings, 18 cars and an educational institution were damaged as a result of the attack, head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration Mykhailo Semikin said.
Russia continues energy attacks, Kyiv says

U.S. President Donald Trump announced on Oct. 11 that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an "energy ceasefire" in the 4 1/2-year-old war, but offered no details on it and Kyiv reported attacks by Moscow on energy sites after his statement.
Ukraine confirmed Thursday it had resumed attacks on Russian oil after a three-day hiatus.

blocks.text: Zelenskyy was outraged by Russia’s continuing aerial bombardment of his country’s energy infrastructure in apparent defiance of Trump’s demand last Sunday for both sides to halt those attacks. The Ukrainian government initially said that it was heeding the ceasefire.
In a post on X Sunday, Zelenskyy said that in the week since Trump’s announcement of an energy ceasefire, Russia had attacked Ukraine’s energy, oil and gas sectors 76 times.
